sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Franklin County, Florida?
sections.html:
Three separate offices touch a Franklin County tax bill: the property appraiser sets the value, the tax collector mails and collects the bill, and the clerk of court runs any tax deed sale. Taxing bodies such as the county commission, the school board and the two cities set the rates.

Franklin County sits in the northwestern Panhandle, about 80 miles southwest of Tallahassee, and covers 545 square miles. The county website describes a population above 11,000 and names two municipalities, Apalachicola and Carrabelle. The county was established in 1832. A house outside those two cities falls under the Board of County Commissioners for its services.

  • Property appraiser: values every parcel, accepts exemption applications, and mails the August TRIM notice. The office does not set tax rates and does not collect taxes. Its website is franklincountypa.net.
  • Tax collector: office at 33 Market Street, Suite 202, Apalachicola, phone (850) 653-9323. It prints bills, takes payment, and runs the certificate sale for unpaid real estate tax.
  • Clerk of the circuit court: holds tax deed sales when a certificate holder applies, and records the deed you sign when you sell.

sections.h2: What are the Franklin County property tax dates?
sections.html:
The property appraiser's calendar starts on January 1, when exemption and agricultural classification filing opens, and the application deadline is March 1. Tangible personal property returns are due April 1. TRIM notices go out in August, and the office says plainly that the notice is not a bill.

The tax collector says statements are mailed on or before November 1. Payment in November earns a 4 percent discount, December 3 percent, January 2 percent and February 1 percent. After that the bill is at face value through March, and the tax becomes delinquent on April 1.

sections.h2: What millage rates does the Franklin County tax collector list?
sections.html:
The tax collector's millage page lists a table headed "Franklin 2025 millage", broken out by taxing unit and printed in decimal form. Ask the tax collector for the current-year table before you plan around these figures, since the published table carries the 2025 label.

  • County: .00504590
  • School, required local effort: .00194400
  • School, discretionary: .00224800
  • Northwest Florida Water Management: .00002070
  • Carrabelle: .00750000
  • Apalachicola: .00834570
  • Dog Island: .00400000
  • Eastpoint district: .00375000
  • Alligator Point: .00123040

The county, school and water lines apply across the county. The city and district lines apply only where the parcel sits, so a house in Apalachicola carries a different total from one on Dog Island or at Alligator Point. The parcel search on the tax collector's site shows the exact lines for your address, and non-ad valorem assessments appear on the same bill.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and caps lower a Franklin County bill?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value for a permanent residence. The first $25,000 applies to all taxes, including school taxes, and a second layer of up to $25,000 applies to value above $50,000 for non-school taxes, per the Department of Revenue homestead guide.

Apply with the Franklin County property appraiser by March 1, and the home must be your permanent residence on January 1. Renting the home out ends the exemption. Once you have homestead, the Save Our Homes cap limits yearly growth in assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The same Revenue guidance says a sale resets the property to just value the next January 1, so a buyer's first bill can be well above yours.

Two other items matter to sellers. Portability lets an owner carry part of the Save Our Homes benefit to a new Florida homestead if it is established within three years of January 1 of the year the old homestead was given up. Owners 65 or older may also qualify for a local additional exemption if the county or city adopted one, so ask the property appraiser whether Franklin County has.

sections.h2: How do I pay, spread out or defer the tax?
sections.html:
The tax collector accepts payment at its Apalachicola office, and the parcel search on the collector's site is the place to see an exact balance. If you pay through a mortgage escrow account, the lender normally pays the bill and you receive an information copy.

Florida also allows installment prepayment under s. 197.222, with the application due to the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year according to the state taxpayer page. The statewide homestead deferral, filed on Form DR-570 by March 31, covers the portion of tax above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. Call the tax collector at (850) 653-9323 to ask whether either plan fits your account before the dates pass.

sections.h2: What happens when Franklin County tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Real estate tax turns delinquent on April 1, and a 3 percent penalty is added. The collector advertises unpaid parcels in the local paper once a week for three weeks in May, and the cost is added to the bill. Unpaid personal property carries 1.5 percent per month instead.

On or before June 1 the collector sells tax certificates online. Bidding opens at 18 percent and goes down, and the lowest bid wins. A certificate is a lien, not a sale of your house. The collector page says a certificate holder who is not paid within 22 months can lose the owner the property at a tax deed sale, and the glossary says the holder may apply for a deed two years after April 1 of the year of issue.

Homestead parcels with under $250 owed are not sold to the public. They go to the county and carry 18 percent interest per year until the balance passes $250.

sections.h2: How does a Franklin County tax deed sale work?
sections.html:
The clerk's office runs the sale. Franklin County sales, when scheduled, are generally held on the first Monday of the month at 11:00 AM inside the main courthouse at 33 Market Street, Apalachicola, and the clerk tells people to call to verify before attending. Notice runs in the Apalachicola Times once a week for four weeks.

  • You can redeem by paying the tax collector before the sale, or before the clerk receives the winning bidder's full payment.
  • For homestead property, the opening bid adds half of the latest assessed value to the taxes, interest and fees.
  • The winning bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is greater, and pays the balance within 24 hours.
  • Documentary stamps of $.70 per $100 of the bid and recording fees are due from the bidder.
  • Some government liens survive the deed, and every property is sold as is.

sections.h2: What should I know about taxes when selling a house in Franklin County?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax is a lien that must be cleared for the buyer to get clean title. If you owe, the closing agent can pay the county tax collector from your proceeds, but a delinquent bill also carries the 3 percent penalty and advertising cost, so ask for a payoff figure dated to your closing day.

Florida collects documentary stamp tax on a deed at 70 cents per $100 of consideration in every county except Miami-Dade, and all parties are liable regardless of who agrees to pay, per the Department of Revenue. The clerk collects it when the deed is recorded. Ask the closing agent for the settlement statement early so the tax lines are clear. A cash buyer can often close without a lender's timeline, which helps when a tax deed deadline or an April 1 delinquency is close.

faqs.q: When are Franklin County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are mailed on or before November 1 and the tax becomes delinquent on April 1. Paying in November earns a 4 percent discount, December 3 percent, January 2 percent and February 1 percent, per the tax collector.

faqs.q: Who sets the Franklin County millage rate?
faqs.a: The taxing bodies set it, not the property appraiser. The county commission sets the county rate, the school board sets school rates, and Apalachicola, Carrabelle and the special districts set their own, per the tax collector's millage page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Franklin County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax is paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the tax collector at (850) 653-9323 for a payoff that includes any penalty and advertising cost, and give it to the closing agent.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a homestead exemption in Franklin County?
faqs.a: March 1 of the tax year, filed with the property appraiser. The home must be your permanent residence on January 1.

faqs.q: Can the county take my house over a small tax bill?
faqs.a: Not quickly. A certificate sale comes first, a holder must wait two years after April 1 of the issue year to apply for a deed, and you can redeem before the sale. Homestead parcels with under $250 owed are not sold to the public.
